- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.
- After a sharp price spike (forecast > 85), model often overshoots and fails to correct; cap forecast at +5% above recent peak or use 3-period moving average.
- If sentiment turns negative (≤0.33) within 3–5 days, model overreacts; apply downward bias of 2–4% for 2–3 periods ahead.
- Model underestimates mean reversion in downward trends; if 3 consecutive days show falling prices, forecast should be adjusted upward by 1–2% to avoid premature bottoming.
- For 30-day horizon, model often overweights recent volatility; use 12-period exponential smoothing or 20-day moving average to dampen noise.
- If sentiment history shows alternating +/– cycles (e.g., +0.67, -0.33, +0.67), model tends to misalign with sentiment direction; align forecast slope with sentiment trend direction.
